job.title: L&D Consultant
job.description:
The Organisation

Our Client is an established and highly regarded organisation operating across the premium retail sector.

With a strong presence across Australia and New Zealand, the business is recognised for its commitment to quality and delivering an exceptional customer experience. It offers a professional, welcoming and collaborative working environment, with a strong emphasis on its people, company values and long-standing reputation.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Learning & Development professional to take ownership of learning initiatives across the business, combining creative content development, engaging facilitation and a passion for building employee capability.

The Team

Joining a small, close-knit People & Culture function, you will work closely with the Head of HR and partner with senior stakeholders across Retail, Client Services and broader business functions.

The team operates in a friendly and collaborative environment, offering a high level of support whilst encouraging individuals to take ownership of their responsibilities and contribute ideas.

You will have the opportunity to build strong relationships across the business, working closely with leaders to understand learning priorities and deliver initiatives that support employee development and business performance.

The Opportunity

This is a broad, hands-on Learning & Development position offering the opportunity to design, develop and deliver engaging learning experiences across a premium retail environment.

With existing learning foundations in place, you will have scope to contribute fresh ideas, enhance training programs and take creative ownership of learning content and delivery.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Designing, developing and facilitating engaging learning programs across retail and internal teams
  • Creating and enhancing product knowledge, sales capability and customer experience training
  • Developing and refining employee induction and onboarding programs
  • Partnering with key stakeholders to identify learning needs and deliver tailored development initiatives
  • Facilitating interactive face-to-face workshops and training sessions
  • Developing digital learning content and maintaining learning resources through the organisation's learning management platform
  • Continuously reviewing and improving learning materials to reflect evolving business needs
About You

You will be an experienced Learning & Development professional who enjoys combining creative instructional design with engaging, hands-on training delivery.

Ideally, you will bring experience from a premium retail environment, with exposure to product knowledge, sales capability or customer experience training. However, experience within other product-led, customer-focused environments will also be relevant.

You will have strong instructional design and content development skills, with the confidence to independently create learning materials and deliver engaging face-to-face training. You will be naturally curious, with the ability to learn new product information and communicate it clearly to different audiences.

The successful candidate will bring excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to engage with employees, managers and senior stakeholders.

Above all, you will be warm, personable and approachable, with a genuine passion for learning and development. You will enjoy taking initiative, contributing creative ideas and making a positive impact within a collaborative team.

The Process

The interview process will include an initial meeting with a Levyl team member, followed by interviews with members of the people team and senior stakeholders.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Harry Hobson on 0461 425 404 or harry@levyl.com.au.

We make selection and shortlist decisions based on your skills, experience, personal attributes and motivators. job.title: Work Health and Safety Manager
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a leading Australian FMCG business that has established a strong reputation and presence within the health and wellness industry!
Founded over a decade ago, the business has experienced significant growth, building an impressive market position through innovation, quality and a commitment to delivering exceptional customer experiences.

With ambitious plans for continued growth, this is an exciting time to join an organisation recognised for its entrepreneurial spirit and commitment to finding better ways of doing things. Behind its success is a passionate team, a fast-paced operational environment and a culture that encourages collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.

Joining as the Work Health & Safety Manager, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of the safety function, influence business-wide safety practices and make a meaningful impact on the wellbeing of employees across the organisation.

The Leaders

Reporting directly to the Chief People Officer, you will sit within the People & Culture team and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, operational leaders and employees across manufacturing, warehousing and logistics.

As the business's key WHS advisor, you will be trusted to provide practical, commercially considered advice, influence decision-making and build the capability of leaders to take ownership of safety within their teams.

The Opportunity

As the WHS Manager, you will lead the development and delivery of the organisation's WHS strategy, taking ownership of safety management systems, risk mitigation, compliance and injury management across a dynamic, multi-site operational environment.

This is a hands-on yet strategic opportunity, where you will have the autonomy to drive continuous improvement, strengthen existing safety frameworks and embed a proactive safety culture throughout the business.

Working closely with stakeholders at all levels, you will play an instrumental role in ensuring the organisation not only meets its legislative obligations but continues to evolve its approach to physical and psychosocial safety.

You will have the opportunity to take ownership of:
  • Developing and delivering a multi-year WHS strategy, driving measurable improvements in safety performance and business-wide initiatives.
  • Leading the implementation and continuous improvement of WHS management systems aligned to ISO 45001, ensuring strong governance, compliance and audit readiness.
  • Identifying, assessing and mitigating operational risks across manufacturing, warehousing and logistics, including machinery, manual handling, hazardous chemicals and workplace traffic.
  • Driving the organisation's approach to psychosocial risk management, partnering with People & Culture and operational leaders to create a safe and supportive working environment.
  • Leading incident investigations, workplace inspections and risk assessments, ensuring effective corrective actions and sustainable safety improvements.
  • Overseeing injury management, workers compensation and return-to-work programs, including complex physical and psychological injury cases.
  • Partnering with senior leaders to provide meaningful WHS insights, reporting and recommendations that support informed decision-making.
  • Leading WHS consultation, safety committee initiatives, training and coaching to build leadership capability and encourage accountability at every level.
About You

You will bring a strong track record of experience in Work Health & Safety within an FMCG or food manufacturing environment, with proven experience operating at a senior or management level, alongside a Diploma in Work Health & Safety or higher.

You will have a proven track record of developing WHS strategies, managing safety systems aligned to ISO 45001, and navigating NSW WHS legislation, including psychosocial risk management. Experience managing complex injury and return-to-work cases will also be essential.

Above all, you will be a confident and influential communicator, with a proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to translate complex safety requirements into practical initiatives that drive meaningful change.
This opportunity will suit someone who is equally comfortable engaging with teams on the production floor as they are presenting safety insights and strategic recommendations to senior leadership.

This is an onsite position, requiring five days per week in the office/site.

The Process

Including an initial consultation with a Levyl consultant, the interview process will involve meeting with key stakeholders to further explore your experience, leadership approach and alignment with the organisation.

For further information, please contact Emilia Rodriguez on 0497 938 177. We look forward to hearing from you!

job.title: P&C Business Partner 12 Month FTC - Up to $150K Package
job.description:
The Organisation

Levyl is partnering with a well-established, privately owned Australian construction business to appoint an experienced HR Business Partner for an initial 12-month fixed-term contract. The organisation continues to grow rapidly, supported by a strong pipeline of major projects. This role will sit within the organisation’s Major Projects division, which delivers large-scale projects typically across two to five-year project lifecycles.

With longer project timelines and highly connected teams, the People & Culture function plays an important role in supporting leaders and employees throughout the full employee lifecycle. The organisation genuinely values its People & Culture team and provides its Business Partners with the opportunity to become closely embedded within their client groups, rather than operating at arm’s length.

This is a great opportunity to join a growing, family-owned business where decisions can be made quickly, strong performance is recognised and there is genuine opportunity to make an impact.

The Team

You will join a large and established People & Culture function that supports circa 950 employees across the business. Within the generalist Business Partnering team, there are a number of HR Business Partners, including  Senior HR Business Partners, with portfolios divided geographically across the organisation.

You will work closely with an experienced HR leadership team and partner with leaders across a designated portfolio within the Major Projects division. The broader team operates collaboratively, while each Business Partner is trusted to build strong relationships and take ownership of their individual business groups.

The organisation’s HR Business Partner model is deliberately high-touch, with Business Partners expected to become a genuine point of contact for leaders and employees and provide proactive support across the full range of people matters.

The Opportunity

As a HR Business Partner, you will take ownership of a portfolio of around 150 employees across three major projects and work closely with leaders and employees throughout the full employee lifecycle.

This is a genuinely hands-on and relationship-focused Business Partnering role. You will spend time within your business groups, understand what is happening across the projects and build the credibility required to provide practical and commercially considered people advice.

The role will combine day-to-day business partnering with broader employee experience and organisational initiatives. You will support leaders across performance, capability, engagement, remuneration, employee relations and workforce planning, while also contributing to projects designed to strengthen the broader employee experience.

Specific responsibilities will include:
  • Building strong relationships with leaders and employees across your designated portfolio.
  • Providing advice and coaching across the full employee lifecycle
  • Supporting performance reviews, career conversations and capability development.
  • Managing employee relations matters, grievances and broader people issues.
  • Supporting annual remuneration reviews and related manager conversations.
  • Working with leaders on employee engagement plans and initiatives
  • Supporting talent management, succession planning and learning and development activity.
  • Contributing workforce insights to support planning and broader business decisions.
  • Supporting employee experience and broader People & Culture projects.
  • Working closely with leaders to improve relationships, engagement, productivity and retention.
  • Collaborating with the wider People & Culture team across business-wide initiatives.
The role is designed to operate as a true partnership with the business, supporting leaders across both strategic and operational priorities while remaining closely connected to employees.

About You

This role would be well suited to an experienced HR Business Partner who enjoys being close to the business, building trusted relationships and working within a fast-paced environment where there is plenty happening.

You will bring demonstrated experience operating at HR Business Partner level across a broad generalist portfolio and be comfortable supporting leaders through the full range of people matters. Strong capability across employee relations, performance, engagement, workforce planning and core People & Culture processes will be important.

This is a role for someone who genuinely enjoys being embedded within their client group. You will be visible, accessible and comfortable spending time with leaders and teams to understand what is happening within the business!

The Process

The interview process will include an initial meeting with a Levyl team member, followed by a first-stage interview with members of the People & Culture leadership team, which may be conducted virtually or face-to-face.

The final interview will be held face-to-face with senior People & Culture leadership.
